output.name: Ketrasa — The Salt Wife's Lamp
output.myth: Mesket's husband took his boat out past the Leeward rocks in the autumn gales, and the sea kept the boat and the man. Mesket did not weep where the children could see. She filled a sack with salt, slung it on her back, and every month walked the cliff path to the strait and rowed across to the skerry wives, who had cod and no salt. Hesk notched each crossing into her reel. When Mesket was old, she tied a lamp to her mast and went out one last time. Orrun felt the small weight of her and did not shrug. She went down into the strait with the salt still on her back, and came up as a lamp. Her light hangs over the place he went under. To her south-east the Bailing Gourd floats over a mother bailing with her children when Tavo came laughing, and to her south-west the Lantern Boat runs after Aun's loose kite. Up north, the Child's Box-Kite pulls at its string above the shingle, and Mesket watches the tide that took the girl. Do not ask her to stop.
output.finding: Find the Child's Box-Kite, Tiskel, and go one hand-span due south of it, where Ketrasa hangs as a lamp over the Leeward water.
